purpose: Proposals to review and choose between before anything is implemented. Nothing on this page is approved. The decision column is deliberately blank and is the reviewer's step.
ranking_basis: impact x 0.5 + confidence x 0.2 + unblocking x 0.3, each scored 1-5; the components are shown so the ranking can be argued with.

decision_rules.rule: One decision per suggestion, recorded as accept, reject or defer. Blank means undecided.
decision_rules.why: So a reviewer can see at a glance which proposals have been touched.

decision_rules.rule: A proposal whose depends_on has not been accepted cannot be accepted.
decision_rules.why: S06 cannot be built before S01; accepting it early would create a task with no input.

decision_rules.rule: Accepting a proposal does not accept its result.
decision_rules.why: Acceptance buys the experiment, not the finding.

decision_rules.rule: Every accepted proposal must name the gate it is expected to clear.
decision_rules.why: So progress is measured on gates, not on completed tasks.

decision_rules.rule: A rejected proposal stays on the page with its reason.
decision_rules.why: So the same idea is not re-proposed every session.

suggestions.title: Obtain official inactive lists for one season
suggestions.discovers: Who was actually unavailable on game day, per club per week — the datum every availability claim depends on.
suggestions.evidence: 347 injury rows and 171 designations are already parsed; 0 games have an inactive list. The ablation arm is empty for exactly this reason.
suggestions.cost: medium: 272 lists for a season, or 18 for the remaining 2026 weeks
suggestions.risk: The lists are the publisher's, so the same section 1.3 limit applies to any automated collection; this would be read, not harvested.
suggestions.acceptance: For at least 100 games, every player marked Out on the report appears on the inactive list (or a stated reason is recorded).

suggestions.title: Turn the report into a multi-day series with hashes
suggestions.discovers: How a designation evolves between Wednesday and kickoff, which is the actual injury signal.
suggestions.evidence: 3 dated captures exist; a delta needs two reads of the same scope.
suggestions.cost: low if read manually once a day; blocked if automated by section 1.3
suggestions.risk: A manual read is a person in the loop, which the brief forbids; an automated one needs consent. This is the sharpest conflict in the brief and it is a decision, not a task.
suggestions.acceptance: Two consecutive daily captures of the same scope, differing in at least one designation, with both hashes retained.

suggestions.title: Add a second, independent season to the corpus
suggestions.discovers: A season-level holdout, which is the only clean out-of-sample device this project can afford.
suggestions.evidence: One season, 120 scored games, and a ranking that changes between two halves of it.
suggestions.cost: high: a second season of scores is 272 more rows, each needing a source page
suggestions.risk: A second season doubles the work and may show the current signal was a one-season artefact. That is a reason to do it.
suggestions.acceptance: The evaluation ranking is computed on season A and reproduced on season B without any parameter change.

suggestions.title: Publish a pre-kickoff forecast ledger for the rest of 2026
suggestions.discovers: The first genuinely prospective record in this repository.
suggestions.evidence: The model exists; the corpus exists; nothing has been recorded before a kickoff.
suggestions.cost: low: 13 rows for Week 11 and 13 a week thereafter
suggestions.risk: The inputs are prior results only, so the Weeks 11 forecast would be weakly informed; publishing a weak number is still better than publishing none, if it is labelled.
suggestions.acceptance: 13 timestamped forecasts exist with a timestamp earlier than the first kickoff of the week.

suggestions.title: Capture one Game Book per game to fix who actually started
suggestions.discovers: The official starting line-up, which is the only way the 'expected versus actual' graph can be closed.
suggestions.evidence: Six depth charts show expected; nothing shows actual.
suggestions.cost: high: one document per game, in a format that is not always text-extractable
suggestions.risk: Game Books are large PDFs; extracting a starting line-up reliably is a parsing project of its own.
suggestions.acceptance: For 10 checked games, the Game Book's starters match an independent official statement of the same starters.

suggestions.title: Reconcile the prior desks' claims against a single fresh read
suggestions.discovers: Which inherited claims are still true today.
suggestions.evidence: Two claims re-read this session did not reproduce (Baltimore's quarterback row, Washington's empty slot).
suggestions.cost: medium: every claim in every desk, one by one
suggestions.risk: A claim that fails because the publisher updated a page looks identical to a claim that was wrong when written.
suggestions.acceptance: Every claim carries a re-read date and a verdict of reproduced / did-not-reproduce / unreadable.

suggestions.title: Register a permitted price source with opening and closing numbers
suggestions.discovers: The market number, without which no residual, ROI, CLV or reward can exist.
suggestions.evidence: The repository's own price desks hold closing observations from a secondary publisher; none is registered here.
suggestions.cost: high: a licence conversation, not a fetch
suggestions.risk: Paying for a feed before the signal is validated would put cost ahead of evidence.
suggestions.acceptance: One game shows a stored open, a stored close, and a residual computed against both, from a source whose terms permit it.

suggestions.title: Verify the depth-chart route for the remaining 26 clubs
suggestions.discovers: Which clubs publish a parseable chart at all, and what each club's slot vocabulary is.
suggestions.evidence: 26 of 32 are already known to serve text (the prior desk said so); 1 is known to serve an image; the rest are unread by this desk.
suggestions.cost: low: 26 page reads and a parser adapter per club
suggestions.risk: Club pages change shape without notice, so each adapter needs a row-count pin or it will silently publish blanks.
suggestions.acceptance: 32 of 32 clubs parse with a pinned slot count and a recorded print date.

suggestions.title: Score the designations against inactive lists once S01 exists
suggestions.discovers: The empirical meaning of Questionable, Doubtful and Out, with intervals.
suggestions.evidence: 90 Questionable and 11 Doubtful rows in one week; no outcome for any of them.
suggestions.cost: medium, and fully dependent on S01
suggestions.risk: A play rate estimated on one season will be confounded by player quality: stars are listed more and play more.
suggestions.acceptance: A play rate per designation with a 95% interval over at least 200 player-games per cell.

suggestions.title: Pin every parser to a schema and a row count, and fail loudly
suggestions.discovers: A build that cannot publish a silently wrong table.
suggestions.evidence: This desk pins 347 injury rows, 172 depth slots, 136 game rows and 13 fixtures; a drift already caught two of this desk's own bugs.
suggestions.risk: A pin that is too tight fails on a legitimate update and trains a reviewer to ignore the failure.
suggestions.acceptance: A deliberate one-field deletion from a saved page fails the build with a named field and source.

suggestions.title: Publish the residual against the benchmark for every originated game, on a schedule
suggestions.discovers: The size and direction of the model's disagreement with a fixed benchmark, tracked over time.
suggestions.evidence: The residual is already computed per game; it is the trend that is missing.
suggestions.risk: A residual against a model benchmark can be mistaken for a residual against a market. The label has to be unmissable.
suggestions.acceptance: Four consecutive weeks of residuals with the benchmark stated on every page.

suggestions.title: Add a roster/IR sweep so 'not listed' stops meaning 'unknown'
suggestions.discovers: Who is unavailable because of a reserve placement rather than because of an injury designation.
suggestions.evidence: The Week 10 report does not list Lamar Jackson; without the reserve list that absence is unexplained.
suggestions.cost: medium: 32 roster pages with a reserve section
suggestions.risk: Roster pages carry a status column that changes shape; a missed section would silently make players look available.
suggestions.acceptance: For 32 of 32 clubs, a reserve list whose count reconciles with the club's own published roster size.

suggestions.title: Write down the price-data policy as a signed decision, not a note
suggestions.discovers: A record of who decided what about price data, so the blank columns stop being ambiguous.
suggestions.evidence: The policy is currently implied by the blank cells.
suggestions.risk: A written policy can be read as a permission. It has to state the opposite: what is forbidden.
suggestions.acceptance: A dated policy file naming the forbidden uses and the person who decided.

suggestions.title: Build the cross-side mismatch matrix for the six charted clubs' opponents
suggestions.discovers: An offence-versus-defence station comparison, which needs both clubs' charts simultaneously.
suggestions.evidence: Six charts are in hand; their Week 10 opponents are not among them.
suggestions.cost: low: read six more club pages
suggestions.risk: A single week's chart against a single week's chart is confounded by scheme and by who actually played.
suggestions.acceptance: Six paired charts, each with a printed date, producing a matrix with no blank cell that is not explicitly gated.

suggestions.title: Register a weather and stadium register before touching totals
suggestions.discovers: Wind, precipitation, roof and surface, which are the standard explanations for a total moving.
suggestions.evidence: The total model is flat (0 total entries distinguishable from the benchmark); weather is a plausible reason to revisit it.
suggestions.risk: Adding features to a model that has no signal yet is the classic way to manufacture one. This should follow S07, not precede it.
suggestions.acceptance: A totals model that improves on the benchmark out of sample *and* whose improvement is attributable to the weather term in an ablation.
